rationale: r2gaussian-claude-agentic: val_n=214, gs_n_gaussians=512, gs_n_iter=400, gs_lr_pos=0.005, gs_lr_scale=0.01, gs_lr_amp=0.01, gs_lr_rot=0.01, gs_amp_init=0.01, gs_scale_init=0.04, gs_tv_weight=0.0001, gs_n_clip=0.05, gs_init_from_fbp=False, gs_outer_wall_s=1080, rationale=iter-2 (search-20260619-01). ONE KNOB: gs_n_iter 150->400 (per-scene Adam steps; all other knobs held at iter-1). FAILURE MODE iter-1: SSIM 0.7383 < LD-FBP baseline 0.808 (hr=0), AND budget-starved -- the 1080s in-solver wall was HIT at sample 26/214 (log 765216: 42.4 s/scene = 282.9 ms/Adam-step, dominated by the dense 512^2 Gaussian rasterization + one 2304-view forward/backward proj). So iter-1 was BOTH under-fit per-scene AND covered only 12% of the 214 slices. HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable in NUMBERS): the 0.7383 is per-scene UNDER-FIT, not a structural ceiling -- 2.67x more Adam steps will lift per-scene SSIM materially above 0.738 (the discarded 20260614 run reached SSIM 0.89-0.92 at gs_n_iter=6000 on val_n=20). FALSIFIER: if the ~9 scenes that finish at gs_n_iter=400 score <=0.76 SSIM (no material lift over 0.738), under-fit is REFUTED and 0.738 is a per-scene structural ceiling. BUDGET MATH: 282.9 ms/step x 400 steps = 113.2 s/scene; 1080s outer wall / 113.2 = ~9/214 scenes finish (well within the 20-min train+score budget; SLURM --time=00:30:00 has headroom, figure excluded). val_n stays 214 (NOT reduced); the per-scene loop self-truncates at the 1080s wall and scores whatever completed -- exactly as iter-1. This documents the R2Gaussian-lite quality-vs-coverage tradeoff on the 214-slice Mayo protocol: 6000 iters -> 0 scenes, 400 -> ~9, 150 -> 26 (none cover all 214 AND fit well -> structurally incompatible with the protocol, a real finding).
